title: Intelligent Sampling of Extreme-Scale Turbulence Datasets for Accurate and Efficient Spatiotemporal Model Training
problem: Training on massive datasets is energy-intensive and slow; Moore's law end means efficiency gains must come from data strategy
motivation: Extreme-scale DNS turbulence data requires new approaches; post-Dennard scaling era demands efficiency rethinking
method: The SICKLE framework uses maximum entropy sampling, a technique that selects the most diverse and informative data points from the dataset—instead of random selection, it prioritizes examples that represent the full range of system conditions. The approach is evaluated against two alternatives: purely random sampling and phase-space sampling (selecting from specific regions of possible states). By intelligently curating which data the model trains on, this method reduces both the dataset size needed and the computational energy required.
key_novelty: Maximum entropy sampling intelligently selects the most representative training data, reducing both dataset size and computational energy costs, as validated on the Frontier supercomputer.
contributions: Introduces MaxEnt sampling for turbulence datasets
limitations: Specific to turbulence datasets; generalization to other domains unclear
